metadata.note: The Missouri and North Arkansas - the 'North Arkansas Line' - ran 365 mi from Joplin, Mo., to Helena, Ark., across the Ozarks, plus stub spurs into Eureka Springs and Berryville. It grew from the Eureka Springs Railway (Seligman - Eureka Springs, 1883), taken over in 1899 by the St. Louis and North Arkansas, which extended it to Harrison (1901), Leslie (1903), Neosho and Kensett (1908) and Helena (1909). Through trains used Kansas City Southern track Joplin - Neosho and Frisco track Wayne - Seligman; those legs are drawn on the host railroads' track in this company's colour, because the map draws who ran the trains. Features are one per section x operator, matching the report's drawable spans: sections with different spans are kept apart, and contiguous sections with identical spans are merged (Harrison - Gilbert + Gilbert - Leslie; Joplin - Neosho + Neosho - Wayne + Wayne - Seligman). Leslie - Kensett is split at Heber Springs because only Leslie - Heber Springs has 1945 evidence. All operations stopped in September 1946; the last passenger train is not dated, so every Missouri and Arkansas feature ends at its last CONFIRMED year (1938 or 1945) and is marked [OPEN].
metadata.ownership_split: Three companies, three colours (Rule 4). (1) Eureka Springs Railway 1883-1899, a separate company conveyed to new St. Louis owners. (2) 'Missouri and North Arkansas' 1899-1935, covering the St. Louis and North Arkansas (1899-1906), the Missouri and North Arkansas Railroad (1906 foreclosure reorganization) and the Missouri and North Arkansas Railway (1922 post-strike reorganization) as one company - reorganizations of the same road. (3) 'Missouri and Arkansas' (Missouri and Arkansas Railway, organized April 1935 to take over the foreclosed M&NA, bought by Frank Kell) 1935 to the end. The research report flagged the 1935 change as a judgement call (UNRESOLVED [U9]) and recommended treating it as one company; the maintainers RESOLVED IT AS A SPLIT, because a new corporation with new owners operated the trains under its own name. Every section spanning 1935 is therefore two features with identical geometry; the boundary year 1935 appears in both, as in ulster_delaware_railroad.geojson.
metadata.geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), routed with opstrace.py (old_railway_operator=M&A covers most of the M&NA grade; M&NA on a few ways near Gilbert; KCS and Frisco for the trackage-rights legs). OpenHistoricalMap queried for the lifted gaps at Heber Springs, Searcy, Kensett, the Cache River and Helena: nothing there. OSM relation 6691528 ('Missouri & Northern Arkansas RR', the modern freight road on the ex-MoPac White River line) is a different railroad and was not used. Traced 2026-11-04.
metadata.traced_vs_documented: Joplin - Helena through route traced 61.4 + 16.0 (Seligman - Junction) + 48.8 + 54.9 + 62.5 + 33.2 + 79.4 = 356.2 mi against 368.0 mi by Fowler's mileposts, which include the in-and-out runs to Eureka Springs (2.52 mi each way) and Berryville (1.81 mi each way), about 8.7 mi; on a like-for-like basis the trace is within about 1% of the documented distance. Spurs: Eureka Springs 2.0 mi traced (2.52 documented), Berryville 2.1 mi traced (1.81 documented). Approximated (straight-line) legs total 14.9 mi, listed by name in each feature's geometry_quality; about 23 mi near Heber Springs is a mapper's reconstruction under Greers Ferry Lake.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends - all Missouri and Arkansas features: Junction - Harrison and Leslie - Heber Springs end at 1945 (Fowler 1945 working timetable); Seligman - Eureka Springs, Freeman - Berryville, Harrison - Leslie, Heber Springs - Kensett, Kensett - Helena and Joplin - Seligman end at 1938 (system-level June 1938 motor-car purchase). These are last-confirmed years, not known ends. All operations stopped September 1946.

[U1] The last passenger train is not dated anywhere. An ICC accident investigation (No. 3018) 'near Harrison, Ark., Aug. 23, 1946' could prove 1946 passenger service if it concerns a passenger train or motor car; not retrieved. Whether Kensett - Helena passenger service resumed after the April-October 1945 White River washout, and whether the KCS trackage rights into Joplin carried passengers to the end, are unknown. Best sources: James R. Fair, 'The North Arkansas Line' (1969); the Aug 1946 ICC report; 1946 Harrison/Searcy/Helena newspapers.
[U2] Eureka Springs Railway to St. Louis and North Arkansas: May 1899 (Encyclopedia of Arkansas) vs 1900 (Shiloh Museum); drawn at 1899.
[U3] ESRy opening: 1 Feb 1883 (ICC valuation, EoA) vs 1882 (Wikipedia ES&NA, probably the charter year); drawn from 1883.
[U4] Harrison - Gilbert (built 1902) and Leslie - Searcy (before the Kensett connection, 1908): passenger opening dates within the year not found; Harrison - Leslie drawn from 1903.

[U7] No headway or running time is sourced for any year; every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this file is an estimate. The 1930 public timetable on condrenrails.com would give a 1930 frequency if someone reads its times.
[U8] Kansas City - Helena Pullman sleepers (EoA): years unknown; north of Joplin they were KCS-hauled and are not drawn.
1921-23 strike: whether passenger service was wholly suspended during the 1921-22 shutdown is not sourced; spans are drawn unbroken per the report's drawable fields.
Station-level stops are not drawn (no stations layer entries).
omitted: Arkansas and Ozarks Railway (Seligman - Harrison with the Eureka Springs and Berryville spurs, Feb 1950 - May 1960): RULE 1 - the Feb 1952 Official Guide reads 'Operated for freight service only ... Aug., 1951' and daggers its stations; no passenger evidence at any date (report block [12], [U6]). Drawable NONE.

Eureka Springs and North Arkansas Railway (tourist, Eureka Springs - Junction, established 1981): no dated excursion year verified - 1981 is the incorporation year and no dated schedule was seen (report block [13], [U11]). Drawable NONE until a dated season is found; it would be its own company and colour with mode tourist_rail.

Helena and Northwestern (Helena - Cotton Plant, Oct 1949 - Nov 1951) and Cotton Plant - Fargo Railway (1952-1970s): no passenger evidence; omitted for lack of a confirmable passenger year (report [U5]), not as proven freight roads.
1946-1949: nothing ran at all; no segment bridges it.
metadata.existing_layer_findings: No existing feature drew this railroad (grep for North Arkansas, M&NA, Missouri and Arkansas, Eureka Springs Railway and the station towns found only unrelated or context hits). Note for a later pass, not changed here: kcs-southern-belle in shreveport_railroads.geojson has only one vertex between latitudes 36.8 and 37.15, so its Joplin - Neosho stretch is a coarse chord lying up to ~9.7 km off the KCS track traced here.

segments.note: Eureka Springs Railway (Powell Clayton's company), a spa branch from the Frisco at Seligman, Mo., to the resort of Eureka Springs, Ark., via Beaver (White River bridge) and Junction. Opened 1 Feb 1883 per the ICC valuation (125 ICC 639, Val. Docket 511) and Encyclopedia of Arkansas; Wikipedia's ES&NA article says 1882, probably the charter year (report UNRESOLVED [U3]). Public timetables of 6 Mar 1886 and 18 Nov 1889 survive (condrenrails.com). Conveyed to the St. Louis and North Arkansas in May 1899 (Encyclopedia of Arkansas; Shiloh Museum says 1900 - report UNRESOLVED [U2]); drawn to the earlier year. Service continued without a break under the new company (see missouri-and-north-arkansas-seligman-eureka-springs). headway_min is an estimate (about two trains each way a day); no frequency is sourced for any year (report UNRESOLVED [U7]).
sources: Segment-level: start 1 Feb 1883 from the ICC valuation and Encyclopedia of Arkansas; passenger service proven by the 1886 and 1889 ESRy public timetables; end 1899 is the conveyance to the StL&NA (Encyclopedia of Arkansas), as established in research/branches/missouri_and_north_arkansas_railroad.txt (researched 2026-11-04) block [1].
